chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: Garland Wilson's club in Paris and Gerard Pochonet
summary: In Paris she worked Garland Wilson's club, then walked out unpaid; drummer Gerard Pochonet got her money and took her to the country. The tape ends.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I worked there for a while, for about I guess a month. Garland Wilson was there and he passed away, he died, you know. It's a place where the customers that really frequent this place didn't like women, but I got in because I was a friend of his. Mr. Orion that owned this place liked me also because he was crazy about Garland. So I got a job there for about 2 months. I was doubling at the theatre, making money. All the Americans had gone back to America and they had so many things for you to do because they had only one left and that was me. All of a sudden I just put everything down and walked off and left

my salary and that's the worst thing you can do in Paris because you'll never get it. But I ran into a wonderful drummer, Gerard Pochonet. He used to play for all the Americans when they came over. He was on a newspaper and everything so he got my money and everything else, you know, for me. He took me out to his house in the country to stay with he and his grandmother.
We're at the end of your tape, so I: This is beginning to imitate you; I'm going to stop. End tape 3
